reconcile.note: Gill reconciles the order by noting Matthew's angel was already seated on the stone, guiding the women in before they themselves found the tomb empty.

discrepancy.note: Strauss says Matthew alone has the angel appear before the women see the empty tomb, while the other Gospels have them find it empty first.

quotes.text: there may appear to be a difference, at … least between Matthew and the three other Evangelists. According to the latter, as they approach and look towards the grave, they see that the stone has already been rolled away by an unknown hand … In Matthew they receive this information before they enter into the grave, from the angel, who after rolling away the stone had sat upon it.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on the order of discovery at the empty tomb, Matt. 28:5 and Luke 24:3.

sides.snippet: I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
sides.verseText: The angel answered the women, \"Don't be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.

sides.snippet: entered in, and didn't find the Lord Jesus' body.
sides.verseText: They entered in, and didn't find the Lord Jesus' body.
